title: useEffect Hook
summary: useEffect lets you perform side effects in functional components — data fetching, setting up subscriptions, or manually changing the DOM. It runs after the component renders. The dependency array controls when the effect re-runs: an empty array [] means it runs once after mount; listing dependencies means it re-runs when those values change; omitting the array means it runs after every render. Return a cleanup function to tear down subscriptions or timers.
keyPoints: useEffect(() => { ... }) — runs after every render (rarely wanted)
useEffect(() => { ... }, []) — runs once after the first render (mount)
useEffect(() => { ... }, [dep1, dep2]) — re-runs when dep1 or dep2 change
Return a cleanup function: useEffect(() => { const id = setInterval(...); return () => clearInterval(id) }, [])
Cleanup runs before the effect re-runs and when the component unmounts
Common uses: fetching data, event listeners, timers, document title updates
Effects run after render, not during — they do not block the browser paint

exercises.prompt: Which useEffect runs only once when the component mounts?
exercises.explanation: An empty dependency array [] tells React this effect has no dependencies, so it only needs to run once after the initial render.

options: Never — it is a static effect
exercises.explanation: The dependency array [count] tells React to re-run this effect whenever the count value changes between renders.

options: It runs before the effect runs for the first time
It clears the interval when the component unmounts
It prevents the effect from running
exercises.answer: It clears the interval when the component unmounts
exercises.explanation: The function returned from useEffect is the cleanup. For a mount-only effect ([]), cleanup runs when the component unmounts. This prevents memory leaks from lingering intervals.

options: The effect runs once on mount
The effect runs after every render
exercises.answer: The effect runs after every render
exercises.explanation: No dependency array means the effect has no way to know when to skip. React runs it after every render, which is rarely what you want.

options: It creates an infinite loop — updating count triggers re-render, which re-runs the effect
count is not accessible inside useEffect
exercises.answer: It creates an infinite loop — updating count triggers re-render, which re-runs the effect
exercises.explanation: The effect depends on count and also sets count. Every render triggers the effect, which changes count, which triggers another render — infinite loop.

exercises.prompt: Which is the correct way to fetch data on mount?
exercises.explanation: useEffect's callback cannot be async directly (it must return undefined or a cleanup function). Use .then() chains or define an async function inside and call it.

exercises.prompt: Complete the effect so it updates the document title whenever count changes:
exercises.explanation: Listing count in the dependency array tells React to re-run the effect whenever count changes, keeping the document title in sync.
